content:
Facts: Life-insurance beneficiary died leaving two wills: first (amended multiple times) leaving warehouse to certain grandchildren, movable co-property to husband's grandchildren conditionally upon beneficiary's predecease or usufruct appointment; second appointing insurance-policyholder universal heir; dispute whether insurance proceeds fell under first will's "movable co-property" bequest versus legitimate succession.
Legal Framework: Articles 457(2), 588, 682 Italian Civil Code (testamentary-legitimate succession concurrence; universal versus particular dispositions; tacit revocation); case law on institutio ex re certa (Cass. 1800/1964, 974/1999, 24163/2013, 9467/2001).
Principles Applied: First will operative when condition-c satisfied (beneficiary appointed usufructuary); second will non-revocatory as deceased intended first-will beneficiaries benefit only if policyholder predeceased (precluding universal-heir appointment). First-will additions effectively post-dated it versus second will. Insurance proceeds excluded from first-will "movable co-property" bequest; deceased specified only jointly-owned sums; excluded solely-held accounts and especially post-will-drafted insurance capital. Extra-textual interpretation-elements permissible only clarifying will-emerged intention, never reconstructing entirely-unexpressed intention. Assessment whether bequests versus heir appointments per Art. 588. Specific-asset indication not necessarily requiring particular-succession/legacy classification. Art. 588(2) requires assessing whether deceased intended assigning indicated assets as estate-portion or not; twofold investigation: objective (deed content) and subjective (testator intent). Extrinsic-element reference permissible if testator-relevant (personality, mentality, culture, social status, environment); successor-behavior/succession-declaration irrelevant for interpretation (purely fiscal value). Doubt-resolution favors legacy classification; Art. 588(2) text merely "not excludes" specific-asset indication may qualify universal disposition only "when appears" estate-portion assignment intent. Absent certain/apparent assignment-intent, specific-asset indication excluded from universal disposition; constitutes particular disposition per Art. 588(1). Institutio ex re certa presupposes assets considered relationally to total-estate value enabling ex-post fraction reconstruction; requires proportional relationship reference between individual bequests and total estate value. Total-assets reference point: will-drafting time (not death-time) respecting testator's consideration at drafting; Art. 588 refers "assets" not "inheritance" indicating value reference excludes succession-totality. Will containing only legacies creates testamentary-legitimate succession coexistence per Art. 457(2); legitimate succession coexists when deceased undisposed entire estate by will, particularly will without heir-appointment containing only legacy attributions.
